senses.gloss:
Rayi is the common word for ‘wealth’ in the Rigveda^1 and
later.^2 Special mention is often made of wealth in ‘heroes’
(vīra) — i.e., in ‘good sons,’^3 in horses,^4 in cattle,^5 etc.
1) i. 73, 1; 159, 4; ii. 21, 6; iii. 1,
19; iv. 2, 7; 34, 10; 36, 9; vi. 6, 7;
31, 1, etc.
2) Av. iii. 14, 1; vi. 33, 3; vii. 80, 2;
Taittirīya Saṃhitā, vii. 1, 72; Vāja-
saneyi Saṃhitā, ix. 22; xiv. 22; xxvii. 6,
etc.
3) Rv. ii. 11. 13; 30, 11; iv. 51, 10, etc.
4) Rv. v. 41, 5; viii. 6, 9, etc.
5) Rv. v. 4, 11, etc.

Rāyo-vāja is the name of a seer of Sāmans or chants in the
Pañcaviṃśa Brāhmaṇa (viii. 1, 4; xiii. 4, 17; cf. xxiv. 1, 7).
